title: Between Formal Recognition and Clinical Practice: A Documentary Analysis of Midwives’ and Nurse-Midwives’ Professional Autonomy in Childbirth Care
content: Background/Objective: Professional autonomy is central to midwifery practice and the provision of woman-centred childbirth care. However, formal recognition of professional competencies does not necessarily ensure their implementation within healthcare organisations. This study aimed to examine how international and Portuguese regulatory and policy documents conceptualise, support and potentially constrain the professional autonomy of midwives and nurse-midwives in childbirth care. Methods: A qualitative documentary analysis was conducted using a purposively selected corpus of 41 publicly available documents published between 2005 and 2026 (22 international and 19 Portuguese documents). Document selection and extraction were informed by the methodological framework proposed by Moilanen et al., and data were interpreted using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Five final themes emerged from the analysis: 1) Regulation legitimises and defines professional autonomy; 2) Competence underpins the authority to make decisions; 3) Professional autonomy embodies a woman-centred model of care; 4) Autonomy requires an organisational environment that makes it possible; 5) There remains a gap in autonomy between legal recognition and practice. Conclusions: International and Portuguese documents broadly recognise the importance of midwifery autonomy, although differences emerge in the extent to which regulatory recognition is translated into explicit organisational responsibilities and models of care. The findings highlight the importance of regulatory clarity, supportive organisational arrangements, professional leadership and interprofessional collaboration. Further empirical research is required to examine how these documentary frameworks are enacted in clinical practice.
